correctness.rationale: The greedy-arch equivalence gives a finite continuation-state recurrence S_j=1+uzE+z S_{j+1}, E=1+z(S_1+S_2); solving gives the exact rational series. Its all-R coefficient polynomial proves support and leading coefficient two, implying exact forcing thresholds. A separate direct-subsequence exhaustive checker tested 26,598 admissible words; an independent state automaton checked 57,036 coefficient cells through length 96. Endpoints and R=1 verified; finite code does not establish the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Three inspected, directly relevant primary texts establish greedy arches, remainder methods, and RLL counts, but not the two-sided run-constrained universality-index distribution. Six targeted published-finding corpus queries compared aliases, finite-R generating functions, broader coverings and exact tables; the closest published and related published results address unrestricted indices, insertion distance or only one-sided run caps. Concrete same-weight/same-run examples show the RLL literature's data does not determine the index. Remaining risk of an unlocated equivalent source is acknowledged.
residual_risks: Uninspected RLL automata or constrained-subsequence literature may contain an algebraically equivalent all-R formula under different nomenclature.
The full texts were inspected in their relevant sections, not every appendix line; textual and page evidence supports the scoped comparison, not an exhaustive negative literature proof.

value.rationale: Homopolymer constraints are central to runlength-limited storage strings, while subsequence universality quantifies worst-case scattered-pattern completeness. The result resolves the naturally cross-classified infinite family for all length, universality levels and homopolymer caps, and proves sharp universal forcing and exactly two boundary exceptions for every pair of parameters. It is not a finite spot check or a mere substitution into an unrestricted distribution.
